title: Psychologist spends six hours inside Tower of London for paranormal investigation
excerpt: A psychologist has spent six hours inside the Tower of London after dark for a paranormal investigation.
content:
A psychologist has spent six hours inside the Tower of London after dark for a paranormal investigation.

Dr Ciarán O'Keeffe, a professor at Bucks New University and one of relatively few parapsychologists in the UK, explored the historic fortress for a Halloween special of the BBC podcast Uncanny.

He gathered accounts of unexplained experiences from those who live and work at the site, including the Yeoman Warders.

Dr O’Keeffe said: "The Tower was different to any other investigation I've done, partly because of its reputation, but also because it's still effectively a military establishment.

"When you go in in the evening after the tourists have gone, and the big door closes behind you, that's it.

"You can't leave.

"And it’s eerily quiet – you know you're in the centre of London but it’s quiet and calm."

The Tower of London is famously believed to be haunted by figures such as Anne Boleyn, Catherine Howard, and Lady Jane Grey – all executed there – and has long been the subject of ghost stories.

Dr O’Keeffe added: "The number of staff and Yeoman we spoke to – they had all sorts of stories that were effectively about ghostly intruders.

"The credibility of these witnesses [Yeoman are required to have served in the British Armed Forces] – they’re not that easily shaken.

"These are individuals who are among the toughest people I've met, who have faced some incredibly challenging and often horrific instances and they're now facing an ethereal figure that they don't know what to do with."

As a psychologist, Dr O’Keeffe considers how the Tower’s dark history might shape perceptions.

He said: "If I suggest to you a place is haunted, you're more likely to have those experiences.

"So if you feel a breeze on the back of your neck, you're looking around for the ghost.

"And of course, we all know the dark past associated with the Tower of London."

Dr O’Keeffe follows a systematic approach to investigations, starting with plausible scientific explanations such as environmental factors, sleep-related phenomena, or psychological influences.

He said: "My typical method is that I will have a list of natural explanations based on the way that experience is described."

The episode featuring his investigation will be available on BBC Sounds and YouTube from 6pm on October 31, before airing on BBC Radio 4 at 9pm.
